title: region-tailored-demotion-heuristic-and-page-grain-defrag-sweeper
author: Elena Morales
description:
Context and motivation: In production we observed pathological spill behavior when long-lived large KV items fragmented hot pages; aggressive eviction forced large synchronous spills that upset token-level latency SLOs and increased downstream IO bursts. This PR introduces a two-pronged approach: 1) a region-tailored demotion heuristic (a lightweight, cost-aware score that demotes cold entries into a 'shadow' region instead of immediate eviction/spill) and 2) a page-grain defragmentation sweeper that opportunistically compacts fragmented pages during low-util windows. Together these reduce unnecessary spills and improve tail latency under mixed workloads.

What changed (high level):
- New demoter: src/kv/demotion.cpp/h implements a compact scoring model that factors recent access recency, tenant weight, estimated spill size (bytes), and estimated kernel copy cost. Rather than evicting immediately, entries that cross the demotion threshold are moved into a lightweight shadow region inside the KV arena. Shadow entries are still addressable (no full roundtrip to object storage) but are flagged for background writeback or final eviction only when IO budget and page pressure allow.
- Page-grain defrag sweeper: src/kv/page_sweeper.cc runs as a low-priority background worker that coalesces small live objects into contiguous pages and frees fully-empty pages back to the allocator. The sweeper uses an adaptive rate limiter (sched-friendly token bucket) so compaction happens only when CPU/io headroom is available.
- Scheduler integration: src/runtime/scheduler.cc adds hooks so demotion and compaction respect runtime batching windows and do not promote items back into hot lanes when they are part of an active continuous-batch session. This prevents churn where hot requests re-promote demoted entries and cause oscillation.
- Kernel/IO budgeting: small adjustments in src/runtime/io_budget.h/cc to link demotion decisions with the IO budget: demoted items are only flushed when budget permits or when the spill queue reaches a high-water mark.
- Tests and benchmarks: tests/kv/demotion_test.cc, benchmarks/kv/bench_demoter.cc add unit tests and microbenchmarks validating correctness and measuring latency/cost tradeoffs.

Implementation notes / design tradeoffs:
- Shadow region is implemented as an allocation bitset overlay, not a second allocator. This minimizes fragmentation risk and keeps promotion/restore cheap (status bit flip + pointer fixup).
- Demotion scoring is intentionally conservative: we bias against demoting small items to avoid moving metadata-heavy tiny keys. The heuristic is pluggable (policy.cfg) for rapid iteration in dedicated clusters.
- Defrag sweeper uses a page-level scan with a configurable compaction window; the default targets pages with <30% live occupancy and prefers tenants with lower active QPS to reduce cross-tenant interference.
- We added tracing spans and metrics (kv.demote.count, kv.demote.restore.count, kv.sweeper.compactions, kv.sweeper.avg_duration_ms) so SRE can tune thresholds post-deploy.

Benchmarks / impact (summary):
- Mixed workload (80% read, 20% write; power-law object sizes) on 8-GPU dedicated cluster: 9.4% average throughput improvement under sustained load and 38% reduction in spill events per hour.
- Tail latency (p95/p99 token latency) improved by ~6–12% depending on workload skew because synchronous spills were avoided.
- CPU overhead for sweeper is <2% on average with default rate limits.

Checklist: 
- [x] New demotion code unit-tested
- [x] Sweeper correctness tests + integration smoke
- [x] Benchmarks added and uploaded to perf-lab
- [x] Metrics/tracing wired to existing telemetry
- [x] Docs: short design note added to docs/kv/demotion.md

Files changed (high level):
- src/kv/demotion.cpp (new)
- src/kv/demotion.h (new)
- src/kv/page_sweeper.cc (new)
- src/runtime/scheduler.cc (mod: hook points + rate gating)
- src/runtime/io_budget.cc (mod: demotion-aware flush logic)
- tests/kv/demotion_test.cc (new)
- docs/kv/demotion.md (new)

Commit summary: 
- c1a3e4b: initial demoter scaffolding and policy config
- c2b4d9f: implement shadow region bitset and fast-promote path
- d5f7aa1: page sweeper implementation + scheduler hook integration
- e6b902d: tests and benchmarks + perf harness config
- f17a3b8: telemetry, docs, and adjust IO budget interactions

Risk and rollback plan:
- The feature is feature-flagged as kv.demote.enabled (off by default). The flag can be toggled via runtime config and will revert behavior instantly without data loss because demotion only alters metadata flags and background movers. If we see higher-than-expected latency, we will disable the flag, let the background sweeper finish, and then revert the binary.

Related work: ENG-9876 (reduce spill storms), ENG-10312 (tenant-aware allocator tuning). Related PRs: this takes a different approach than previous eager-evictors by introducing a shadow tier and focusing on page-level compaction rather than micro-coalescing every allocation.
review_comments:
Samir Patel: Nice separation of concerns; can you explain how the shadow region bitset interacts with existing slab compaction?
Elena Morales: The bitset is an overlay; we do not change slab headers. During a sweep we materialize relocated objects into contiguous slots and flip bits atomically to avoid races.

Jae Park: The demotion score has a few tunables - can we expose them via runtime config and add defaults for heavy-tenant clusters?
Elena Morales: Yes; policy.cfg exposes score weights and tenant multipliers. I added a note in docs and defaults tuned for dedicated capacity.

Lina Becker: Any regression risk for continuous-batching clients? We saw oscillation patterns in earlier PRs.
Elena Morales: Scheduler hooks prevent immediate promotion while a continuous-batch token is active; tests simulate batching sessions and assert no oscillation.
QA (Arjun): reproducer for spill storm included in bench harness; verified reduction in local perf lab.

Ops (Marta): Please add metrics to the SLA dashboard before enabling in prod.
Elena Morales: Added kv.demote.* and kv.sweeper.* counters and updated dashboard playbook.
release_notes: Reduced unnecessary synchronous spills by introducing a shadow demotion tier and page-level compaction sweeper. Expected improvements: fewer spill events, lower tail latency, and modest throughput gains. Feature is behind kv.demote.enabled flag.
